batchResizer.content.h1: What is Bulk Image Resizing & Why Batch Processing Matters
batchResizer.content.p1a: Resizing multiple images individually is one of the most repetitive, time-consuming tasks in modern digital workflows. Whether you manage an e-commerce store with hundreds of product listings, run a photography blog, or prepare assets for social media campaigns, resizing images one by one slows down your productivity and introduces human error.
batchResizer.content.p1b: The ImgFeel Bulk Image Resizer enables you to upload dozens or hundreds of photos simultaneously, set unified target dimensions or target file size limits, and process all files in a matter of seconds. By leveraging high-performance client-side Canvas rendering, your files never leave your computer, ensuring instantaneous throughput and absolute data privacy.
batchResizer.content.feat1Desc: Upload and resize unlimited photos at once with smooth multi-threaded Canvas interpolation.
batchResizer.content.feat2Desc: 100% client-side processing guarantees your private photos never touch external cloud servers.
batchResizer.content.feat3Desc: Instantly bundle and download all resized images in a clean, organized ZIP archive.
batchResizer.content.feat4Desc: Smart auto-ratio locking ensures mixed portrait and landscape images never stretch or distort.
batchResizer.content.h2: How Bulk Image Resizing Works in Your Browser
batchResizer.content.p2a: Traditional online image resizers require uploading every file over your internet connection to a remote backend server, queuing them in a cloud conversion pipeline, and then downloading the results back. This approach consumes significant bandwidth, poses privacy risks, and creates bottlenecks when processing large batches of high-resolution camera photos.
batchResizer.content.p2b: ImgFeel uses modern HTML5 Canvas technology and high-precision bicubic filtering directly in your browser. When you select your files, your computer's local CPU and GPU process the pixels in real time. Resized files are generated as in-memory binary Blobs and packaged into standard ZIP archives without a single byte sent over the network.
batchResizer.content.h3: Understanding Width, Height, and Aspect Ratios in Batch Resizing
batchResizer.content.p3a: When processing a collection containing photos with different orientations—such as portrait photos (3:4 or 9:16) alongside landscape banners (16:9 or 3:2)—applying fixed width and height dimensions directly to all images can cause unwanted stretching or distortion.
batchResizer.content.p3b: By keeping 'Lock Aspect Ratio' enabled, our tool calculates the proportional height for each individual image based on its unique aspect ratio. For example, if you set a target width of 1200 px, a 16:9 landscape photo will resize to 1200 × 675 px, while a 1:1 square photo will resize to 1200 × 1200 px, keeping all visuals perfectly proportioned.

batchResizer.content.h5: Common Use Cases for Bulk Image Resizing
batchResizer.content.p5a: E-Commerce Catalogues: Standardize hundreds of product photos to uniform dimensions (such as 1200×1200 px or 800×800 px) across Shopify, Amazon, WooCommerce, and Etsy in a single batch.
batchResizer.content.p5b: Real Estate & Photography Portfolios: Downscale massive 24MP and 48MP RAW/JPEG camera exports to web-optimized 1920×1080 Full HD previews without losing visual sharpness or color richness.
batchResizer.content.h6: Pro Tips for Preserving Quality in Batch Resizing
batchResizer.content.p6a: Always start with high-resolution original source files. Downscaling an image retains sharp edges and details, whereas upscaling a small thumbnail beyond its native resolution can introduce pixelation and blur.
batchResizer.content.p6b: For web publishing and blog articles, resizing large 4000px camera photos down to 1200px or 1600px reduces file weight by over 75%, significantly improving your Google PageSpeed Insights score and Core Web Vitals.

batchResizer.faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
batchResizer.faq.q1: How many images can I resize at once?
batchResizer.faq.a1: There is no strict limit. Because processing happens locally in your browser, you can resize dozens or even hundreds of photos at once depending on your device's memory.
batchResizer.faq.q2: Are my uploaded photos sent to any server?
batchResizer.faq.a2: No. ImgFeel is 100% client-side. Your photos never leave your device, ensuring total privacy and security.
batchResizer.faq.q3: Can I download all resized images at once?
batchResizer.faq.a3: Yes. Once the batch resize is finished, click 'Download All (ZIP)' to save all resized photos in a single organized ZIP archive.
batchResizer.faq.q4: Will aspect ratio locking prevent image distortion?
batchResizer.faq.a4: Yes. When 'Lock Aspect Ratio' is checked, each image scales proportionally based on its natural dimensions, preventing stretching or squishing.
batchResizer.faq.a5: ImgFeel supports JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, and BMP formats for both input and output.
batchResizer.faq.q6: Does bulk resizing reduce image quality?
batchResizer.faq.a6: Our engine utilizes high-quality Canvas bicubic interpolation and high-fidelity encoding (92% quality for lossy formats) to ensure images remain crisp and clear.
batchResizer.faq.q7: Can I resize photos by percentage instead of exact pixels?
batchResizer.faq.a7: Yes. Click on quick scale percentage chips such as 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% to scale all images proportionally.
batchResizer.faq.q8: Is this bulk image resizer free to use?
batchResizer.faq.a8: Yes, ImgFeel Bulk Image Resizer is 100% free with no registration, no watermarks, and no usage limits.
